newsitem.title: SPAIN: Spain may make income tax less progressive - Costa.
newsitem.headline: Spain may make income tax less progressive - Costa.

text.p: Spain wants to reform its fiscal system in the coming years and intends to make income tax less progressive and introduce instruments to support savings, Secretary of Exchequer Juan Costa said on Wednesday.

"The government wants to improve the fiscal treatment of savings...to do that means approving measures that reduce income tax progressiveness, or approving instruments which could boost savings, such as pension plans or insurance contracts," Costa said at a two-day economic conference here in Madrid.
He added that in its first months, the centre-right government's fiscal objectives are to modernize the fiscal system and meet the Maastricht convergence criteria.
In coming years, the government would be working to make the Spanish economy and companies more competitive, he said.
Costa added the government has the intention of approving a better fiscal treatment for the small- and medium-sized firms.
He also said the Spanish government intends to extend tax advantages for inheritance of family firms.
